findings.title: Materials' 66-point lens gap signals earnings collapse
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.30x forward but 36.98x trailing, a 66-point percentile gap between the two lenses. That spread implies analysts expect 127 percent earnings growth next year, a bet that the current earnings trough is about to reverse violently.

findings.title: Real Estate's 45-point monthly percentile plunge
findings.body: Real Estate's forward percentile fell 45 points in one month to 7, yet its forward P/E of 33.94 remains the most expensive in the table. The market is marking the sector down on expectations of a 4 percent earnings decline, but the multiple still prices in no such deterioration.

findings.title: Energy's forward percentile cheapens while trailing stays rich
findings.body: Energy's forward percentile dropped 14 points in a month to 47, while its trailing percentile sits at 77. The 30-point gap between lenses shows analysts expect 47 percent earnings growth, but the market is already discounting that optimism in the forward multiple.
